The Raval quarter is located between the left side of the Eixample and the Gótico quarters. It is one of the quarters with more changes in the last years, going from a very popular neighbourhood to a dynamic area where restorers, designers, architects and artists have chosen it a place to settle, making the quarter one of the most dynamic, trendy and multi-ethnical ones of the city, yet without losing its popular charm.

The Museum of Contemporary Art (MACBA), the Centre of Contemporary Culture (CCCB), and the Universities have eased the change of a marginal area to a cosmopolitan one, becoming a reference for all the city.

In the Raval the old and the modern blend naturally; for this we can see how the neighbourhood enjoys all type of facilities, from the most modern ones to the lifelong stores –the great markets of the Boquería or Sant Antoni. Therefore, the traditional, the modern, and the alternative coexist in this quarter in permanent evolution.

name: Sweett | Midtown Fortuny
description: This recently renovated three-bedroom apartment has a welcoming vibe. The fully equipped kitchen will be ideal for preparing a meal for the whole family. The large beds will offer you the best sleep on your vacation. Located in the heart of Barcelona you will find most of the city landmarks within a walking distance such as; Casa Batllò, Plaza Catalunya, and the well-known Las Ramblas street.
neighborhood_overview: A modernist treasure trove full of elaborate and often fantastical buildings, elegant landscapes and upmarket fashion - there’s really something magical about Eixample.  The area sits on the right hand side of Passeig de Gràcia, the main boulevard that separates the city.  Its gridded layout keeps things nice and simple for walking around - most tourists flock to Gaudi’s emblematic Sagrada Familia church, but Eixample itself is a peaceful, residential neighbourhood that offers many an opportunity for a quite respite.  You could easily spend the day just popping in-and-out of the various artist galleries, small boutiques and neighbourhood cafes scattered about, that is if you can tear yourself away from the high-end shops that line the avenues.  To top it all off, Eixample is only two metro stops away from Placa Catalunya at the city centre.

With 10+ years of hosting experience, we ensure a home-like stay with cozy bedding, fast WiFi, and a Nespresso machine. Our 24/7 team assists with early check-ins, transfers, housekeeping, and local tips. Enjoy welcome treats, personalized recommendations, and our smart app. Sweett is your perfect base for urban escapes.

neighborhood_overview:
Our neighbourhood is called Poble Sec and was built in the late 1800s and early 1900s. It is nestled at the foot of Barcelona's hill and park: Montjuic, and boasts many lovely old buildings. It is slightly off to one side and therefore not as overrun with tourists and noise as the Gothic, Borne and Raval areas. Poble Sec is more of a residential area and is a breath of fresh air after being in those areas; its tree-lined streets are much more peaceful, with hardly any traffic. The central pedestrian main street Calle Blai springs to life in the evenings with people hanging out on the terraces of the many popular tapas bars and restaurants which line it.

Our building is located at almost the end of a "cul-de-sac" street a few blocks up from the bustling Calle Blai, so there is very little noise and the apartment is very peaceful and quiet. At the end of our street there are some steps which lead to Montjuic hill and its parks.

The Eixample was designed as a grid by architect Cerdà . It extended from the Plaza Catalunya , in the top of Ciutat Vella , through pastures and fields to the neighboring villages of Sarria and Sant Gervasi and attention in the late 1960s , as Barcelona was expanding beyond the original wall the old town. This construction coincided with the explosion of local wealth , which led to many local families commissioning housing construction modernist architects such as Antoni Gaudí , resulting today in the majestic buildings scattered throughout the Eixample .

Currently , many people consider the Eixample as the true heart of Barcelona, and is one of the most desirable locations to buy a property in Barcelona. In this area there are a lot of shops, galleries , restaurants and bars along its wide , tree lined streets . In the popular Paseo de Gracia there are many of the most exclusive boutiques in the world, among others, Chanel, Louis Vuitton and Burberry .

A place where they could feel welcome, that was nice to stay in, like their home, even more daring, more fun.

A place to rest in a natural environment, a place to read, enjoy the afternoon light or even have breakfast in the light of the sunrise.
A base camp from which to discover the city and its surroundings.

Now we have several units in the city and in nature.
When a guest tells us that they had a great time, it makes me happy. It makes me feel very good that they take away a great memory of the moments lived in our place.
  
I am aware that most of it depends on the mindset of the guest, but maybe a small part also depends on us.

neighborhood_overview:
Poblenou is Barcelona’s creative heart: an underrated area packed with great restaurants, bars and things to do.

Poblenou was the centre of Barcelona’s industrial revolution, and the best way to get to know it is to start at the foot of the neighbourhood: Ciutadella Park, where the touristic artery of Carrer de Pujades turns into a densely inhabited industrial estate. In the surrounding eight blocks, you’ll hardly see any signs of the textile and transport businesses that were built in the ‘Manchester of Catalonia’ in the twentieth century; instead, you come across digital marketing agencies, spectacular co-working spaces, lavish speciality coffee shops and art galleries, all set in massive industrial buildings. And just when you think you’ve stepped into a Catalan-dubbed episode of ‘Portlandia’, you reach the heart of Poblenou’s residential area, a village in itself:  Carrer de Marià Aguiló.

While the Rambla de Poblenou is where you’ll find fewer locals and more

neighborhood_overview:
Barcelona's Eixample district (Ensanche) was built in the 19th century. The birthplace of the Modernisme art movement, whose main figure is Antoni Gaudí.

This area is home to the impressive Sagrada Familia, famous "La Pedrera", Gaudí's work, the Apple of Discord, Hospital de la Santa Creu and Sant Pau, etc.

A large part of the attraction of the Eixample is the mythical Passeig de Gràcia Avenue, one of Spain's most famous avenues due to its importance in shopping, business, and a great showcase of outstanding works of modernist architecture, comparable to Champs Elysées in Paris or Fifth Avenue in New York.

This area is full of excellent modernist buildings, such as the Casa Batlló de Gaudí, the Casa de Puig i Cadafalch Amatller, and Lleó Morera de Domènech i Muntaner known as the Manzana de la Discordia.

The University of Barcelona is also in this area, an elegant building with beautiful gardens and Casa Gofverichs Boada. A Gaudí collaborator

The Eixample, which translates to "expansion" as it is the newest part of the city, is a large area north of Plaça de Catalunya to the left and Passeig de Gràcia to the right.

In fact, this place is an extension of the city that greatly benefited from the ingenious urban planning carried out by the Catalan engineer Cerdá during the 1850s. Cerdá had a weakness for straight lines, which is why the entire area is arranged on a grid and each block has an internal patio. This means that it is very difficult to get lost in the Eixample and, as a consequence, very easy to find places.

Gracia used to be a separate town on the edge of Barcelona until it was absorbed by its larger neighbour. It is renowned for the fact that it has always managed to maintain an independent character from the rest of the city.

Gracia offers the choice of quiet sleepy side streets alongside the life and bustle of its squares.

host_about:
Apreciado huésped.

Si bien mi pareja y mi familia, son por supuesto importantes para mí, puedo decirte que mi piso y mi huerto son dos de las cosas más importantes en mi vida, donde se refleja toda mi personalidad, clásica para muchos y poco convencional para la mayoría.  

No me apasiona viajar como turista, si integrarme en otra ciudad como uno más en una actividad profesional pues he viajado mucho por trabajo.

Sí me apasiona acoger...

Cuando de niña, en el colegio había una nueva compañera, mi pasión era recibirla, enseñarle el colegio, explicarle los detalles que necesitaba, hasta que la nueva compañera encontraba sus nuevas amigas y yo seguía con las mías... 

Ya de mayor... desde siempre compartí mi piso, procurando que siempre, todos los compañeros de piso estuvieran lo mejor posible.  

Puedo decir de mis compañeros de piso, que han aportado bonitas cosas y otros fueron complicados... pero en general he tenido una buena relación con ellos.  Todos nos hemos caracterizado por lo que yo llamo... "el  saber hacer y saber estar" en piso compartido.. Principalmente de esos periodos recuerdo LAAARGAS tertulias de noche, casi nunca se encendía la televisión.    

Ahora mi piso empieza una nueva etapa, lo hemos actualizado y hemos hecho algo que nos ha apasionado, hemos recuperado el suelo de mosaico hidraulico origina y por tanto refleja más que nunca la verdadera intención del arquitecto al construirse....

Podrás disfrutar de lo que yo disfruto de él, su luz incluso en días de lluvia, las vistas al cielo, a la sagrada familia, a las copas de los árboles y lo que en casa llamamos el "petit Paris" las buhardillas de algunos edificios al otro lado del parque. 

En definitiva, podrás disfrutar de lo más grande que yo tengo... mi pequeño, coqueto y gran piso.  Espero que estés bien y puedas gozar de una buena estancia en Barcelona.

The Eixample / Ensanche or the "expansion", was the area of the city developed when the walls of the Old Town/Amurallada were torn down in the mid-19th century. Built on a flat screen pattern of Ildefons Cerdà. The Eixample contains most of the great modernist buildings, including several works by Gaudí and its contemporaries Puig i Cadafalch and Domènech i Montaner, as well as less famous architects. There is a Route of Modernism, developed by Turismo de Barcelona that guides you around the modernist treasures of Barcelona and other cities.

You could easily spend the day just popping in-and-out of the various artist galleries, small boutiques and neighbourhood cafes scattered about, that is if you can tear yourself away from the high-end shops that line the avenues. neighborhood_overview: NEIGHBORHOOD: Sant Antoni is a neighborhood in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Catalonia (Spain). Its non-official center, the marketplace of the same name—designed by Antoni Rovira i Trias and built between 1872 and 1882—is one of the oldest and most popular in the city, especially with the secondhand book stalls that surround the building Sunday mornings. It is bordered by the neighborhoods of the L'Antiga Esquerra de l'Eixample (on the other side of Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes), the Raval (on the other side of Ronda de Sant Antoni), and Poble Sec (on the other side of Avinguda del Paral·lel). The streets of Sant Antoni follow the grid pattern prevalent in all of Eixample, except for a central thoroughfare, the Avinguda de Mistral, built on the site of an important medieval road which lead out of Barcelona. Another well-known landmark of Sant Antoni is the bar called Els Tres Tombs, right next to the market.

L'Eixample is still mostly upper-middle class and is characterized by nice shops and wide quiet streets. Its uniquely modernist character makes it a fascinating place to meet. Nearly all of the architectural attractions of the late 20th century are located in
l'Eixample.

Antoni Gaudí is one of the most universal figures in Catalan culture and international architecture.

neighborhood_overview:
The Putxet is a core of the newly created Putget and Farró neighborhood in the Sarriá-San Gervasio district of the city of Barcelona. Before 2007, this neighborhood was administratively separate from El Farró.
The name comes from the homonymous mountain, which 135 meters high is located in the center of the neighborhood. It is bordered by Avenida de la República Argentina, Calle Claudi Sabadell, Calle de Marmellà, Calle de Roca i Batlle, Padre Fidel Fita Street, Calle de Musitu, Calle de Bertrán, Calle de Balmes, the round of General Mitre and Lesseps Square.
The neighborhood began to develop in 1850 as a result of the extension of Gràcia towards Collserola and today it is mainly occupied by upper-middle class neighbors. Mount Putget was urbanized and became an urban park in 1970.

In 1882, the original Sagrada Família Gothic church project, designed by Francesc de Paula Villar, was taken over by the young Antoni Gaudí, who transformed it into the most fascinating church of all time. An architectural bible called the Sagrada Família which has become a Barcelona icon. The building, which is still under construction, has lent its name to the area and made it world famous. host_about:
HOLA! We are a welcoming, respectful and friendly couple: Pere is a secondary school teacher (now retired), and Xavier is a university teacher (now retired as well). We really like to share our space.  We both love the people who live in Barcelona, as well as the wide and variety offer of this city, although neither of us were born here.
We would like to offer you the possibility to discover the multiple Barcelonas that coexist, especially those who are far from what you can see in every magazine or tourist guide. If you want to see them all, contact us!

Some of the attractions we can share are visual and audio-visual art exhibitions, bookstores and libraries, and theatre venues. We are always ready to see any type of theatre play. One of our common aspects of our shared life is the natural tendency of hosting family and friends in our home. For us, is crucial to always have a room available for hosting those who want to visit our city and hang out with us.
We enjoy hosting people, and we prefer to meet people within their cities, rather than see just cities with people. As Blaise Pascal would say: “happiness is a marvellous thing: the more you give, the more you are left with”.
Have a great day. Cheers!

neighborhood_overview:
The Gothic Quarter (Catalan: Barri Gòtic and Spanish: Barrio Gótico) is the centre of the old city of Barcelona. It stretches from La Rambla to Via Laietana, and from the Mediterranean seafront to Ronda de Sant Pere. It is a part of Ciutat Vella district.
Despite several changes undergone in the 19th and early 20th century, many of the buildings date from Medieval times, some from as far back as the Roman settlement of Barcelona. Remains of the squared Roman Wall can be seen around Tapineria and Sots-Tinent Navarro to the north, Avinguda de la Catedral and Plaça Nova to the west and Carrer de la Palla to the south. El Call, the medieval Jewish quarter, is located within this area too.
The Barri Gòtic retains a labyrinthine street plan, with many small streets opening out into squares. Most of the quarter is closed to regular traffic although open to service vehicles and taxis.

Barcelona's Eixample district (Ensanche) was built in the 19th century. The birthplace of the Modernisme art movement, whose main figure is Antoni Gaudí.

This area is home to the impressive Sagrada Familia, famous "La Pedrera", Gaudí's work, the Apple of Discord, Hospital de la Santa Creu and Sant Pau, etc.

A large part of the attraction of the Eixample is the mythical Passeig de Gràcia Avenue, one of Spain's most famous avenues due to its importance in shopping, business, and a great showcase of outstanding works of modernist architecture, comparable to Champs Elysées in Paris or Fifth Avenue in New York.

This area is full of excellent modernist buildings, such as the Casa Batlló de Gaudí, the Casa de Puig i Cadafalch Amatller, and Lleó Morera de Domènech i Muntaner known as the Manzana de la Discordia.

Somos una familia con tres hijos maravillosos, dos de ellos viven con nosotros y la mayor se va a estudiar a otra ciudad. 
Ser parte de nuestra familia durante tu estancia es la mejor oportunidad para conocer el estilo de vida, la cultura y la gastronomía de nuestra ciudad. Disfrutarás del buen ambiente del corazón de Pamplona. 
No vemos las cadenas de televisión, pero vemos muchas películas. Nos encanta leer y la naturaleza. Creemos que Airbnb nos da la oportunidad de que personas maravillosas puedan compartir con nosotros un trocito de su vida. neighborhood_overview: Sant Antoni is a neighborhood in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Catalonia (Spain). Its non-official center, the marketplace of the same name—designed by Antoni Rovira i Trias and built between 1872 and 1882—is one of the oldest and most popular in the city, especially with the secondhand book stalls that surround the building Sunday mornings. It is bordered by the neighborhoods of the L'Antiga Esquerra de l'Eixample (on the other side of Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes), the Raval (on the other side of Ronda de Sant Antoni), and Poble Sec (on the other side of Avinguda del Paral·lel). The streets of Sant Antoni follow the grid pattern prevalent in all of Eixample, except for a central thoroughfare, the Avinguda de Mistral, built on the site of an important medieval road which lead out of Barcelona. Another well-known landmark of Sant Antoni is the bar called Els Tres Tombs, right next to the market.

neighborhood_overview:
The Gothic Quarter (Catalan: Barri Gòtic, IPA: [ˈbari ˈɣɔtik], Spanish: Barrio Gótico) is the centre of the old city of Barcelona. It stretches from La Rambla to Via Laietana, and from the Mediterranean seafront to Ronda de Sant Pere. It is a part of Ciutat Vella district.

Despite several changes undergone in the 19th and early 20th century, many of the buildings date from Medieval times, some from as far back as the Roman settlement of Barcelona. Remains of the squared Roman Wall can be seen around Tapineria and Sots-Tinent Navarro to the north, Avinguda de la Catedral and Plaça Nova to the west and Carrer de la Palla to the south. El Call, the medieval Jewish quarter, is located within this area too.

The Barri Gòtic retains a labyrinthine street plan, with many small streets opening out into squares. Most of the quarter is closed to regular traffic although open to service vehicles and taxis.

neighborhood_overview:
Barcelona's Eixample district (Ensanche) was built in the 19th century. The birthplace of the Modernisme art movement, whose main figure is Antoni Gaudí.

This area is home to the impressive Sagrada Familia, famous "La Pedrera", Gaudí's work, the Apple of Discord, Hospital de la Santa Creu and Sant Pau, etc.

A large part of the attraction of the Eixample is the mythical Passeig de Gràcia Avenue, one of Spain's most famous avenues due to its importance in shopping, business, and a great showcase of outstanding works of modernist architecture, comparable to Champs Elysées in Paris or Fifth Avenue in New York.

This area is full of excellent modernist buildings, such as the Casa Batlló de Gaudí, the Casa de Puig i Cadafalch Amatller, and Lleó Morera de Domènech i Muntaner known as the Manzana de la Discordia.

The University of Barcelona is also in this area, an elegant building with beautiful gardens and Casa Gofverichs Boada. A Gaudí collaborator

The massive 22@ plan sets to convert Poblenou into the city's technological and innovation district, as well as to increase leisure and residential spaces.

Alongside the newly built, upscale Vila Olímpica and Diagonal Mar areas, many artists and young professionals have converted the former factories and warehouses into lofts, galleries, and shops. Art & Design schools and studios have also opened, making the area known for its creative outlook.

Some of the old factory buildings are now declared historic monuments and are under protection.

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city, and it is one of the most popular districts in the Catalan capital. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. Eixample Derecho is home to many gems of 'Modernisme' architecture, including the unique Casa Milà (La Pedrera), the colourful Casa Batlló and the towering Sagr

neighborhood_overview:
The beautiful neighbourhood known as the Gothic Quarter is so called because it used to be the Roman village and thus has some remnants of its glorious past. These days because of the constant modernization it is easy to spot an ancient building right next to one built in the 90s. It is this mix of old and new that brings people from all over the world to stay in the Gothic Quarter.
You will be spoilt for choice of restaurants and bars, especially around Plaça Reial which is always full day and night. The night-life in the Gothic Quarter is lively to say the least and you will always find somewhere to have a drink or a dance. Calle Ferran, which is just to one side of Plaça Reial and leads up to Plaça Sant Jaume with its imposing government buildings is also good for bars and cafes.

neighborhood_overview:
Our flat is located only one minute walking from Catalonia Square, the strongly beating heart of Barcelona. A favourite meeting point, it's also the geographical space that separates the districts of Ciutat Vella and the 19th century-built Eixample. Steeped in history, is the nerve centre of the Catalan capital. The Plaça Catalunya, with its large shopping centres and department stores, is constantly teeming with people. It is Barcelona's most central area and a favourite meeting place for locals and visitors. It also connects the Eixample and the old town.

Some of the city's most important streets and avenues meet at Plaça Catalunya: Passeig de Gràcia, Rambla de Catalunya, La Rambla or Portal de l'Àngel, in addition to Ronda de Sant Pere, Carrer de Vergara or Carrer de Pelai. The plaza is especially known for its fountains and statues, its proximity to some of Barcelona's most popular attractions, and for the flocks of pigeons that gather in the centre.

Both Pau & Ewa love meeting people from all around the world. description: This lovely  state of the art apartment is situated right in the centre of Barcelona, just a few minutes´ walk from Plaça Catalunya, in the stylish Eixample neighbourhood. neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. The Parc de Joan Miró, with its iconic 'Woman and Bird' sculpture created by the Barcelona-born artist, is also situated here, as well as the Arenas

neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is right next to Plaça Catalunya, at the heart of the city, on the border between the Gothic Quarter and the Eixample district.

The Eixample was designed as an extension of the historic old town of Barcelona as the city’s population swelled in the 19th century. Urban planners needed to find a solution to the housing crisis and resulting sanitary risks, and so conceived of this grid-pattern neighborhood of modern houses, which would connect with the then-independent villages Sarrià and Gràcia.

As a result, many of the houses in the Eixample date back to the 19th and early 20th century, when the architectural movement known as Catalan Modernism was in full swing. Leading Modernists such as Antoni Gaudí, Lluis Domenech i Montaner, and Josep Puig i Cadafalch all have buildings in the Eixample.

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city, and it is one of the most popular districts in the Catalan capital. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. Ariel Bercovich. Architect, designer and photographer.

Son of a photographer and a school teacher, self-taught, the camera has been his lifelong companion, the eye through which his perception of reality is filtered and blended.

WHAT
In his latest work, he focuses on photographing urban spaces, landscapes and architecture, though he also enjoys doing portraits and taking part in spontaneous collaborations in the world of theatre and communications. 

HOW
His interdisciplinary background has culminated in a unique way of conceptualising space and a natural intuition for transmitting emotions. Ariel's work is characterized by a love for the details, a passion for capturing the essence of everything that moves him and a mastery of technical skills, which enable him to give each photograph an especially high-quality finish.

WHERE
Born in Buenos Aires. Lives in Barcelona. Inspiration: the world.

Ariel Bercovich. Arquitecto, diseñador y fotógrafo.

WHAT
Su obra reciente se enfoca hacia la fotografía de espacios urbanos, paisajes y arquitectura. Aunque disfruta con el retrato y efectuando colaboraciones espontáneas en el mundo del teatro y la comunicación.

La formación multidisciplinar le confiere una particular forma de conceptualizar el espacio y una intuición natural para transmitir emociones. El amor por los detalles y el interés por captar la esencia de todo aquello que le conmueve son los rasgos que definen su obra. Y su gran técnica, el instrumento que le permite otorgar, a cada fotografía, un acabado de grandísima calidad.

neighborhood_overview:
Our flat is located only one minute walking from Catalonia Square, the strongly beating heart of Barcelona. A favourite meeting point, it's also the geographical space that separates the districts of Ciutat Vella and the 19th century-built Eixample. Steeped in history, is the nerve centre of the Catalan capital. The Plaça Catalunya, with its large shopping centres and department stores, is constantly teeming with people. It is Barcelona's most central area and a favourite meeting place for locals and visitors. It also connects the Eixample and the old town.

Some of the city's most important streets and avenues meet at Plaça Catalunya: Passeig de Gràcia, Rambla de Catalunya, La Rambla or Portal de l'Àngel, in addition to Ronda de Sant Pere, Carrer de Vergara or Carrer de Pelai. The plaza is especially known for its fountains and statues, its proximity to some of Barcelona's most popular attractions, and for the flocks of pigeons that gather in the centre.

neighborhood_overview:
The second largest neighborhood in our beloved Barcelona is Sarrià-Sant Gervasi - a quiet paradise in the north-west of the city, bordering with Gracia.

Sarria-Sant Gervasi is renowned as the most expensive neighborhood in Barcelona, and you get what you pay for - the area is filled with green parks, shopping areas, interesting sights, and narrow and quiet streets. This neighborhood has a distinct small-town feeling, making it very special. The greatest aspect of this neighborhood is it's location further from the most touristic parts of the city. The earliest information on Sarrià-Sant Gervasi was contained in a document written in 987, describing the neighborhood's origin as a Roman colony. neighborhood_overview:
Raval is a multicultural mosaic of people from all over the world.
Here, Barcelona’s modernity is fused with the past of the Barrio Chino. At one time it was one of the most densely populated districts of Barcelona, but now after many depopulation plans, the city is removing the underdeveloped parts and replacing them with parks, plazas, cultural centers, and much more.
This used to be an uncomfortable area of Barcelona, but it has turned itself around.
It’s now very charming with many independent shops and home of La Boquería Market, Las Ramblas, El Gran Teatro del Liceo, Museo Marítimo, Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Barcelona (MACBA), Centro de Cultura Contemporánea de Barcelona (CCCB), La Filmoteca, Antic Hospital of Santa Creu, music clubs, small galleries and ateliers, modernist bars and restaurant such as the Confitería, the Almirall or the Marsella.

We are Barbara and Emiliano, a couple from Italy now based in Barcelona since more than fifteen years after having lived and traveled in several countries in the last 25 years.

neighborhood_overview:
The flat is located in the Poble Sec neighbourhood in the Sants-Montjuïc district of Barcelona. This area is known for its wide range of entertainment and bohemian atmosphere.

During the 1920s, the area was an important entertainment centre with theatres and music halls that attracted Barcelona's working class. Today, it is a lively neighbourhood with a wealth of bars, restaurants and shops.

Within walking distance of the flat, you will find tourist attractions such as the Teatre Lliure, the Mercat de Sant Antoni and the Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya. You can also easily walk to the famous Blai street, known for its tapas bars and festive atmosphere.

For food lovers, in and around Carrer de Blesa there are many typical tapas bars and restaurants, such as Cerveseria Catalana, a Barcelona institution, where you can enjoy a wide variety of tapas and local dishes. We also recommend trying the paella at La Tía Cebolla or the patatas bravas at Bar Seco.

description: Beautiful Modernist apartment in Barcelona, restored respecting the original elements (coffered ceilings, modernist windows, hydraulic mosaics ...). Feel how the Catalans lived at the end of the 19th century but with all the modern comforts.
neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is located next to Las Ramblas in Barcelona, one of the city's most historic and lively areas.
However, the few meters that separate us from the Ramblas, make our environment relatively quiet and easily accessible, but very convenient to visit the best known places of Barcelona.
Walking a few meters from the apartment, you will find the century-old Boqueria Market, one of the most famous in the world, with top quality products that we serve in our breakfasts, and where chefs are supplied with Michelin stars.
A few more steps and you will find yourself in front of the façade of the Liceu, one of the world temples of opera, with its exclusive Cercle del Liceu, epicenter of the cultural and economic power of the 19th century.
The main places of interest such as The Cathedral in the Gothic Quarter, The Picasso Museum, the MACBA or the CCCB ... The Palau de la Música, a key piece of Catalan Modernism, or some of Gaudí's star architectural works: La Pedrera

neighborhood_overview:
El Coll is a neighbourhood of Gracia, one of the 10 districts Barcelona is divided in. Located at the base of Tibidabo, it's 300 meters above sea level.
Its history goes back to the 11th century with the construction of the church that bore its name: Esglesia del Coll.
At the beginning of the 20th century, the neighbourhood was filled with "Masies" and houses.
At 60th, El Coll suffered an urbanistic explosion and was invaded by all kind of constructions that took up all free spaces that remained.
This neighbourhood is away from the busy life of the center of the city, but well connected through metro Lines and buses.
There are many parks and green areas, the most famous is the Gaudi’s creation Parc Guell.

host_about:
El entorno dinámico y alegre de la capital catalana se plasma en The Moods Catedral en forma de experiencia de alojamiento cercana y cálida. Desde el trato de nuestro personal hasta la comodidad de la zona común y nuestras 17 habitaciones, todos los ambientes del hostal tienen mucho de Barcelona y del carácter mediterráneo de sus gentes.

Una idiosincrasia que se percibe ya a la llegada a este hotel del barrio Gótico, donde una recepción con techo de volta catalana con ladrillos en blanco y muebles de líneas sencillas en tonos beige dan la bienvenida al visitante. El pavimento textil en tonos tierra a juego con el minimalismo del mobiliario se conjuga a la perfección con paredes blancas no exentas de vegetación y una presencia omnipresente de la madera. El toque final de bienestar lo aportan las cómodas butacas en tela de lino, un lugar donde descansar o tomar algo.

Esta decoración de diseño llena de guiños a la tierra se reproduce a lo largo de todos y cada uno de los espacios. Colores puros, elementos básicos y geometrías simples se repiten en la zona común de este hotel situado en el límite de los barrios del Gótic y el Born.

En esta zona común, a la cual nos gusta llamar Helpyourself por el servicio gratuito de bebidas al cual tienes acceso durante todo el día, encontrarás también una sala donde hojear algunas de nuestras revistas de moda, tomarte algo, trabajar con tu ordenador o simplemente descansar después de una jornada de turismo en la ciudad.

Asimismo, nuestras 17 luminosas y tranquilas habitaciones han sido creadas en un estilo contemporáneo donde la exclusividad no está reñida con la sencillez.

En The Moods Catedral te transportamos a la mismísima esencia del Mediterráneo.

neighborhood_overview:
The neighborhood of Gràcia is just one stop up from the top of Passeig de Gràcia but it feels like a whole different world. Gràcia was an independent town until the late 19th century and even now the community is small and tight. The people are exceedingly proud of their roots, they don't say they come from Barcelona, they say they are from Gràcia.
The area is popular with artists and a generally bohemian crowd. It also has a high ethnic population and the highest concentration of foreign restaurants in Barcelona. Plaça del Sol is the most renowned area of the neighborhood, it's lined with terrace cafés and at night this is where the people convene to drink and be merry.

This place is good for people who want to live a real local experience.

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city, and it is one of the most popular districts in the Catalan capital. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. Eixample Derecho is home to many gems of 'Modernisme' architecture, including the unique Casa Milà (La Pedrera), the colourful Casa Batlló and the towering Sagr

The Eixample, which translates as "widening" because it is the newest part of the city, is a large area north of Plaça Catalunya to the left and Passeig de Gràcia to the right.
The Eixample is famous because there you can find most of Barcelona's art nouveau masterpieces and because it is a high class residential area with many shops.
The right side of the Eixample is the oldest and therefore has a more impressive architecture, although in reality there is no great difference between the two parts.

The Passeig de Gràcia is located in the heart of the Eixample and divides it into two: "the left Eixample" and "the right Eixample".
Here you can find the best international designer stores, such as Chanel and MaxMara. In addition, along this street are La Pedrera and Casa Batlló, two of Gaudí's typical dreamed buildings. The right side of the Eixample is the oldest and therefore has a more impressive architecture, although in reality there is no great difference between the two parts.

neighborhood_overview: The location of our apartment is the edge between the Eixample district and the historic Old Town of Barcelona which makes it a very convenient spot from where to start the daily excursions. Our street is this gorgeous and the city's wealthiest avenue. Here on Passeig de Gracia is where all the famous designer brands have their stores. host_about:
In September 2002, I traveled to Barcelona for the first time. Back then I was 25 years old. I stayed for 10 days and that was enough for me to fall in love with this amazing city. After this trip, I returned to my home country (Germany), packed my bags, made the necessary arrangements, and relocated to Barcelona 4 weeks later. I was only living in my new destination for one week when a local apartment owner asked me if I might know people in Germany who would like to visit Barcelona and rent her apartment for their holiday. And I did. A friendly gesture later turned into a business. Today I own and manage a small and exclusive selection of holiday rentals in Barcelona center. So far, I had the opportunity to host guests from all over the planet; Alaska to Oman, Island to Abu Dhabi, and from everywhere in between. What a great experience. I still remember my first days in Barcelona and therefore understand well how especially first-time visitors feel. There is so much to discover and it gives me great pleasure to not only provide a safe and comfortable place to stay for my guests but also share the rich culture of this unique place. Food, wine, history, and local people are just amazing.
Although I offer holiday rentals for many years, I only started listing on Airbnb recently and I am looking forward to connecting to the community that shares this platform.

The areas are safe and primarily residential but there is much entertainment to be had as well. This includes popular bars, theatre and even a club. In Ciutat Vella you can follow in the footsteps of ancient Romans, pray in Gothic churches reaching for the sky, stroll through the palaces built by the businessmen back from the colonies for their mistresses, follow the trail of the great Modernista architects and enjoy the most contemporary cultural offering in the city in the El Raval neighbourhood.
You can bring ancient professions back to life through street names and even relive the passion of the great artists, from the painter Pablo Picasso to the flamenco dancer Carmen Amaya. Because Barcelona is cosmopolitan and elegant, bourgeois and modern, but it has not lost its essence, of the port and scoundrels, ancient and decadent, that you can still feel in the streets of Ciutat Vella, the first district, where it all started.

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. Carrer Tallers is one of the old medieval streets of the city of Barcelona. It's located on the edge between the Raval north and l'Eixample districts and connects Plaça Universitat with Les Ramblas.
It is a street full of diversity with people of many backgrounds and nationalities, full of fun and very popular.

This street offers all kinds of shops, from second-hand clothing to military stores, music records, instruments or antiques. There are also all kinds of cafes, bars and restaurants such as the emblematic Teresa Carles and Flax and Kale.

In Plaza del Pi, named after the adjoining Gothic church, an art market is installed every weekend.

Barcelona architecture is, in reality, an attraction in itself. Just stroll around the city, especially through our neighborhood: "the Eixample", and you'll find an endless amount of fascinating buildings and unexpected treasures.

From Roman times to the Gothic period to the Catalan Art Nouveau, "modernisme," Barcelona's architecture naturally transmits the city's rich history. It speaks for eras of varying prosperity and decline, for fervent Catalan nationalism or subjugation to the central government, for Expos, Olympic Games, Cultural Forums and more.

The two most important styles of Barcelona architecture are Catalan Gothic, a medieval style, and Modernisme, a turn of the 20th century movement protagonized by Antoni Gaudí.

From Roman times to the Gothic period to the Catalan Art Nouveau, "modernisme," Barcelona's architecture naturally transmits the city's rich history. It speaks for eras of varying prosperity and decline, for fervent Catalan nationalism or subjugation to the central government, for Expos, Olympic Games, Cultural Forums and more.

The two most important styles of Barcelona architecture are Catalan Gothic, a medieval style, and Modernisme, a turn of the 20th century movement protagonized by Antoni Gaudí.

neighborhood_overview:
Barcelona architecture is, in reality, an attraction in itself. Just stroll around the city, especially through our neighborhood: "the Eixample", and you'll find an endless amount of fascinating buildings and unexpected treasures.

From Roman times to the Gothic period to the Catalan Art Nouveau, "modernisme," Barcelona's architecture naturally transmits the city's rich history. It speaks for eras of varying prosperity and decline, for fervent Catalan nationalism or subjugation to the central government, for Expos, Olympic Games, Cultural Forums and more.

The two most important styles of Barcelona architecture are Catalan Gothic, a medieval style, and Modernisme, a turn of the 20th century movement protagonized by Antoni Gaudí.

neighborhood_overview:
Pronouncing its name might be tricky, but getting lost in Eixample doesn't tend to be a problem. This modern area of Barcelona was designed by Catalan civil engineer Cerda in the mid 18th century as the old town area was starting to burst at its medieval seams. Its geometric layout and broad, sunny streets are a pleasant contrast to the labyrinthine feel of the older parts of the city.

The wealthy elite of Barcelonese society were keen to make their mark on this new town, and commissioned some of the most in vogue architects of the day to design their homes. As a result, Eixample boasts the most concentrated example of Modernista architecture in Barcelona. As you are wandering around, don't look at your feet. Peek into doorways and patios and glance up at street lamps and balconies - you'll see lots of little Modernista touches that all go towards creating the atmosphere of the place.

neighborhood_overview:
Located in between the Gothic Quarter and the Ciutadella Park, El Born is one of Barcelona‘s trendiest and most popular neighborhoods. Home to some of the oldest buildings in the city, it is not only one of the most historic areas of Barcelona but also one of its liveliest. Popular with tourists and the local international community, it’s famous for its bo-ho feel and artistic edge as well as its great tapas bars and trendy bistros

Originally a settlement on the outskirts of the old walled city, the Born was incorporated into the city of Barcelona when the walls were extended in the 15th century. Many of the early inhabitants were fishermen and dockworkers, but as time passed, noblemen and rich merchants began to construct houses there, and the neighborhood’s social fabric took on a new dimension. The popular ‘Passeig del Born‘ was once the center of life in the neighborhood, home to market traders as well as street entertainers and day workers.

The streets are always full of people reviewing their daily lives, socializing or chatting with neighbors while sitting in outdoor cafes.
To really have the feeling of the neighborhood, it is worth visiting Gràcia on foot.

neighborhood_overview:
El Carmelo is a neighborhood in the Horta-Guinardó district of Barcelona, ​​located in the upper part of the city. It extends along the hill of the same name, belonging to the foothills of the Collserola mountain range, with a rugged terrain with numerous slopes, which causes steep slopes in numerous streets of the neighborhood.
Formerly it was divided between four towns: Gracia, Sant Joan d'Horta, San Martin de Provensals and San Andrés de Palomar. Between the end of the 19th century and the beginning of the 20th it was a place of second residences for the bourgeoisie of the then village of Gracia. Until the 1920s it had a markedly rural character, with numerous orchards and green areas, a fact that began to change with the arrival of a growing immigration from the rest of Spain. Then, single-family homes gave way to the barracks, while from the 1960s began to build large blocks of housing in the real estate boom of the time, which eventually transformed the face of the neighborh

description: Your hotel in Poble Nou. From our hotel, you can live and feel the pulse of the most authentic day-to-day life of the neighbourhood and enjoy it like a local. The locals' chats on the Rambla del Poblenou, the runners by the sea, the small, traditional shops await you next to your hotel Sallés Pere IV
neighborhood_overview:
A unique neighbourhood

PobleNou was the old industrial area of Barcelona. In the 1960s, it was transformed and opened up to the sea, giving way to design studios, art schools and exceptional restaurants, making it the city's most innovative district and a centre for design and the avant-garde.
Inspiration, design and tradition come together in the streets of PobleNou.
Despite being the city's new fashion and trend district, it has managed to preserve the charm of a traditional neighbourhood alongside the city's most outstanding technology companies, think-tanks, and start-ups.

"Bienvenidos a Sallés Hotel Pere IV, Soy Arturo,

Nuestra oferta  incluye un acceso diario y gratuito al spa, donde tendrán la oportunidad de usar la piscina. De la mano de nuestros expertos terapeutas, disfrutar de diferentes tratamientos , y hacer así conectar su mente con su cuerpo y relajarse en este entorno urbano.
Como complemento le ofreceremos un completo desayuno y una variada oferta gastronómica.
Estoy seguro de que nuestras recién renovadas instalaciones y  los consejos de nuestro equipo, harán de su estancia en Barcelona una inolvidable experiencia."

neighborhood_overview:
Pronouncing its name might be tricky, but getting lost in Eixample doesn't tend to be a problem. This modern area of Barcelona was designed by Catalan civil engineer Cerda in the mid 18th century as the old town area was starting to burst at its medieval seams. Its geometric layout and broad, sunny streets are a pleasant contrast to the labyrinthine feel of the older parts of the city.

The wealthy elite of Barcelonese society were keen to make their mark on this new town, and commissioned some of the most in vogue architects of the day to design their homes. As a result, Eixample boasts the most concentrated example of Modernista architecture in Barcelona. As you are wandering around, don't look at your feet. Peek into doorways and patios and glance up at street lamps and balconies - you'll see lots of little Modernista touches that all go towards creating the atmosphere of the place.

host_about:
In September 2002, I traveled to Barcelona for the first time. Back then I was 25 years old. I stayed for 10 days and that was enough for me to fall in love with this amazing city. After this trip, I returned to my home country (Germany), packed my bags, made the necessary arrangements, and relocated to Barcelona 4 weeks later. I was only living in my new destination for one week when a local apartment owner asked me if I might know people in Germany who would like to visit Barcelona and rent her apartment for their holiday. And I did. A friendly gesture later turned into a business. Today I own and manage a small and exclusive selection of holiday rentals in Barcelona center. So far, I had the opportunity to host guests from all over the planet; Alaska to Oman, Island to Abu Dhabi, and from everywhere in between. What a great experience. I still remember my first days in Barcelona and therefore understand well how especially first-time visitors feel. There is so much to discover and it gives me great pleasure to not only provide a safe and comfortable place to stay for my guests but also share the rich culture of this unique place. Food, wine, history, and local people are just amazing.
Although I offer holiday rentals for many years, I only started listing on Airbnb recently and I am looking forward to connecting to the community that shares this platform.

neighborhood_overview:
From the airport to the hostel you'll have three options: train, bus or shuttle.

Train: In front of Terminal 2 (T2) you'll find a train station where you can get the "R2" train. You'll need to get off in 'Passeig de Gracia' which is a 15 min walk to the hostel. I may suggest you buy the T-CASUAL ticket. It costs 11,35€ and it has TEN RIDES on it. You can use it in all public transports in Barcelona.

Bus:
- During the night: In each terminal you can find a night-bus. Bus N17 from Terminal 1 (T1) and bus N16 from Terminal 2 (T2). Both are going to leave you in Plaça Catalunya which is again about 15 min walking to the hostel.

- During the day: You can take the bus 46 from both terminals. It will take you to Plaça Espanya, where you can take the bus D50 or H12, which are going to leave you at Plaça Tetuan (two blocks away from the hostel)

The ticket costs 2,20€ and you must pay it in cash to the driver.

neighborhood_overview:
Gracia used to be a separate town on the edge of Barcelona until it was absorbed by its larger neighbour. It is renowned for the fact that it has always managed to maintain an independent character from the rest of the city.

The neighbourhood is richly cultural, from the diversity of people walking its streets to street parties, human towers, live music and fireworks, a wide variety of restaurants, and cinemas, theatres and galleries. The unique architecture also adds a charm of its own.

Gracia offers the choice of quiet sleepy side streets alongside the life and bustle of its squares.

name: COSY 2 BDRM URBAN RETREAT
description: This cosy and cute 40m2 2 bedroom apartment, while small, is packed with loads of charm and character, just like the charming working class early 1900s Poble Sec neighbourhood in which it is nestled, a short walk from Barcelona's central street Las Ramblas. There's airconditioning, fast fibreoptic wifi, and a washing machine.
neighborhood_overview: The building is typical of the area, Poble Sec, built in the late 1800s and early 1900s and packed full of character and charm. The neighbourhood itself is nestled at the foot of Barcelona's hill and park: Montjuic, and boasts many lovely old buildings. I consider Poble Sec to be one of Barcelona's "best kept secrets": while still being very central (Las Ramblas is only a 10 minute walk away), it is slightly off to one side and therefore not as overrun with crowds and tourists as the Gothic, Borne and Raval areas. The central pedestrian main street (Calle Blai), just around the corner from the apartment, is hugely popular with the locals and has some great bars and restaurants which spring to life at night. One of my favourite pass-times is to spend evenings on one of the many terraces here and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere and tasty food.

neighborhood_overview:
Getting to know the neighbourhood: “el Poble Sec”
After Barcelona's capitulation to the Castilians in the War of Succession in 1714, the area was declared a military zone and building was prohibited so as not to obstruct the cannon balls fired at the city of Barcelona from the Spanish-controlled Castle on Montjuïc.

However, its proximity to the Port meant that the area began to be industrialised throughout the early 19th century and coal deposits for the port and areas for drying textiles were located here, and similarly, the stone quarry on Montjuic was exploited for city building projects.

Despite its grid format, the neighbourhood was urbanised in a rather disorganised fashion and the name Poble Sec, which means Dry Village, came about because the barri had no running water until 1894.
Electric light was installed along El Paral.lel in 1882 and by the early 20th century, the area was a centre of nightlife with cabarets, theatres and café-concert halls

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. host_about:
In September 2002, I traveled to Barcelona for the first time. Back then I was 25 years old. I stayed for 10 days and that was enough for me to fall in love with this amazing city. After this trip, I returned to my home country (Germany), packed my bags, made the necessary arrangements, and relocated to Barcelona 4 weeks later. I was only living in my new destination for one week when a local apartment owner asked me if I might know people in Germany who would like to visit Barcelona and rent her apartment for their holiday. And I did. A friendly gesture later turned into a business. Today I own and manage a small and exclusive selection of holiday rentals in Barcelona center. So far, I had the opportunity to host guests from all over the planet; Alaska to Oman, Island to Abu Dhabi, and from everywhere in between. What a great experience. I still remember my first days in Barcelona and therefore understand well how especially first-time visitors feel. There is so much to discover and it gives me great pleasure to not only provide a safe and comfortable place to stay for my guests but also share the rich culture of this unique place. Food, wine, history, and local people are just amazing.
Although I offer holiday rentals for many years, I only started listing on Airbnb recently and I am looking forward to connecting to the community that shares this platform.

neighborhood_overview: A modernist treasure trove full of elaborate and often fantastical buildings, elegant landscapes and upmarket fashion - there’s really something magical about Eixample.  The area sits on the right hand side of Passeig de Gràcia, the main boulevard that separates the city.  Its gridded layout keeps things nice and simple for walking around - most tourists flock to Gaudi’s emblematic Sagrada Familia church, but Eixample itself is a peaceful, residential neighbourhood that offers many an opportunity for a quite respite.  You could easily spend the day just popping in-and-out of the various artist galleries, small boutiques and neighbourhood cafes scattered about, that is if you can tear yourself away from the high-end shops that line the avenues. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. neighborhood_overview: A modernist treasure trove full of elaborate and often fantastical buildings, elegant landscapes and upmarket fashion - there’s really something magical about Eixample.  The area sits on the right hand side of Passeig de Gràcia, the main boulevard that separates the city.  Its gridded layout keeps things nice and simple for walking around - most tourists flock to Gaudi’s emblematic Sagrada Familia church, but Eixample itself is a peaceful, residential neighbourhood that offers many an opportunity for a quite respite.  You could easily spend the day just popping in-and-out of the various artist galleries, small boutiques and neighbourhood cafes scattered about, that is if you can tear yourself away from the high-end shops that line the avenues.  To top it all off, Eixample is only two metro stops away from Placa Catalunya at the city centre.

description:
Very nice Modernist apartment completely refurbished luxuriously while respecting the Barcelona style. 140 m2 like a loft, bright and calm, with a south-facing balcony for having breakfast. In the heart of Barcelona, ​​behind the Boqueria Market and the MACBA Museum. A chic apartment to live to the rhythm of the Barcelona movida without compromising on comfort.

neighborhood_overview: El Raval is a dynamic neighborhood with avant-garde exhibitions at the Museum of Contemporary Art and the adjoining Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona. Adorned with street art, the surrounding streets are full of bohemian-style bars and trendy designer boutiques. On La Rambla Avenue, La Boqueria Market offers fish and seafood, wine and tapas, while friendly cafes line Rambla del Raval. The Maritime Museum features replicas of boats in shipyards from medieval times. The Santa Creu Hospital is also a pleasant walk. This former hospital site, now a library surrounded by shady gardens, will make you appreciate the mild Catalan climate, enjoying the view of the magnificent modern and colorful monument.

neighborhood_overview:
Barcelona architecture is, in reality, an attraction in itself. Just stroll around the city, especially through our neighborhood: "the Eixample", and you'll find an endless amount of fascinating buildings and unexpected treasures.

From Roman times to the Gothic period to the Catalan Art Nouveau, "modernisme," Barcelona's architecture naturally transmits the city's rich history. It speaks for eras of varying prosperity and decline, for fervent Catalan nationalism or subjugation to the central government, for Expos, Olympic Games, Cultural Forums and more.

The two most important styles of Barcelona architecture are Catalan Gothic, a medieval style, and Modernisme, a turn of the 20th century movement protagonized by Antoni Gaudí.

Sensi consist of a couple restaurant next to each other. Great tapas place. My favorites are sensi gourmet and sensi bistro tapes.
Vinitus is great as well for tapas.

host_about:
In September 2002, I traveled to Barcelona for the first time. Back then I was 25 years old. I stayed for 10 days and that was enough for me to fall in love with this amazing city. After this trip, I returned to my home country (Germany), packed my bags, made the necessary arrangements, and relocated to Barcelona 4 weeks later. I was only living in my new destination for one week when a local apartment owner asked me if I might know people in Germany who would like to visit Barcelona and rent her apartment for their holiday. And I did. A friendly gesture later turned into a business. Today I own and manage a small and exclusive selection of holiday rentals in Barcelona center. neighborhood_overview:
Barcelona has a plethora of cool neighbourhoods, but in recent years, there’s one barrio that just hasn’t stopped changing and growing. Poblenou lies at the centre of the Barcelona design movement, and attracts everyone from hipsters to start-ups with its trendy markets, concept stores and innovative festivals.

Poblenou is located to the east of the city centre, between the area of Glories and the stunning beach. It used to be a very traditional Catalan neighbourhood, and the central and lower parts of the barrio still are. This area is dotted with colourful Modernista architecture, and even has its own ‘rambla’ (esplanade). The north and surrounding areas, however, are very different, filled with big old warehouses and modern tech hubs. It’s here where hipsters, designers and start-ups have moved in. This area has become known as @22, a place now occupied by design schools, galleries, craft beer breweries, and new-age digital companies looking to take over the world.

The spectacular gothic Cathedral of Barcelona overlooks thriving boutiques and cafés along stone-paved streets that are ripe for exploration and afternoon ambling.  Meandering alleyways and arched passages open to tranquil sunlit plaças and to the teeming avenues of La Rambla and Via Leitana which flank the neighborhood. Intricate wrought-iron street lamps illuminate the quarter as it transforms into its evening splendor. Bars and restaurants burst into activity on flourishing squares like Plaça Reial, while the nightlife crowd spills in and out of the secluded spots of narrower streets.

neighborhood_overview:
Fort Pienc is a neighborhood located in the Eixample district of Barcelona. The area is named after the historic Fort Pius, a fortress that once stood on the site and was demolished in the mid-19th century to make way for the expansion of the city.

Today, Fort Pienc is a residential neighborhood with a diverse mix of cultures and nationalities. The area is known for its beautiful tree-lined streets, spacious squares, and green spaces, such as the Parc de la Ciutadella, one of the largest parks in Barcelona.

Fort Pienc is home to several notable landmarks and attractions, including the Arc de Triomf, a triumphal arch built for the 1888 Barcelona World Fair, and the impressive Auditori concert hall. The neighborhood is also known for its lively food scene, with a range of traditional and modern restaurants serving up delicious Catalan cuisine.

Fort Pienc is well-connected to the rest of the city, with several metro and bus lines running through the area.

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. The Parc de Joan Miró, with its iconic 'Woman and Bird' sculpture created by the Barcelona-born artist, is also situated here, as well as the Arenas

neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is located in the very heart of the Eixample district, specifically in the Eixample Esquerra area. This neighborhood is one of the most iconic and central in the city, known for its grid layout designed by Ildefons Cerdà and its wide, lively avenues. Rambla de Catalunya, in particular, is one of the most elegant and vibrant streets, lined with plane trees and featuring a central boulevard perfect for strolling or sitting at a terrace café. The atmosphere is cosmopolitan, safe, and dynamic, offering a wide range of shops, cafés, restaurants, and boutiques.
Just a few minutes’ walk from this location are some of Barcelona’s most iconic landmarks. Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller, two jewels of Catalan Modernism, are only five minutes away on foot. Passeig de Gràcia, the city’s most luxurious avenue, is very close, filled with high-end shops and historic buildings. Plaza Catalunya, the city’s nerve center and main connection point, is about a ten-minute walk away. The Merc

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. neighborhood_overview:
Gràcia is a one of the most authentic neighborhoods in Barcelona. It is located in the center of Barcelona, but there is a small town feeling wherever you walk, especially in the squares, where the locals spend their free time.

Here you will find a mixture of bohemian, trendy and traditional. This is mirrored in the new design boutiques that thrive everywhere. The gastronomical offer is quite diverse, ranging from take away pizza and sushi restaurants, to high quality catalan food.

Verdi is one of its most iconic streets. Here you can start off with drinks and tapas, then attend a movie theatre and watch a film in original version, have Egyptian food for dinner and enjoy Italian ice cream for dessert.

Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. name: A beautiful room in Guinardo
description:
Hello everybody, welcome to our little house. Our home is like a sanctuary where we take care of our plants, the food we eat, and the vibes.

It is not located in the center of Barcelona, but it's a quiet neighborhood and it's very close to the Barcelona mountains.

PS: Even if you'll have a bunk bed in the dormitory, the use of the room is totally private and for a single person during your stay with us.

PS2: The view is not from the apartment but at 10 minutes' distance walking.
host_about:
Hi everyone!

I'm Edgar, welcome to my place! 

I like to have people from anywhere as long as they can follow the small everyday routines and organization. As a permaculture lover, I like our guests to respect the ecosystem while they are with us. It simply means to use our amenties with moderation and conciousness. We also recycle with separated bins. Taking care of the appartment where we live and the people (we are 3), is also very important. 

Another important thing for us is that we are not a hostel. We want you to have the best experience with all the comfort that our little home can give you. But as we are are going to live with you for a few days we also like to be aknowledged (just a simple "Hi! How are you?" is enough). The main thing is that we want to feel that you are sharing with us your experience.  

Thanks for reading. 
We are looking forward to meeting you!

Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. At the foot of Montjuïc is Poble-sec. The history of this neighborhood of the Sants-Montjuïc district dates back to the mid-19th century, when it was a rural area, with vegetable gardens and farmers' huts. In 1850 it began to be populated by families, especially immigrants, who could no longer fit in the Raval, and who worked in the large number of textile factories that were installed in the area.

Apart from the characteristic activity, which positioned Poble-sec as one of the niches of the industrial revolution, the neighborhood has also always been associated with the world of entertainment. Emblematic theaters such as El Molino, the Apolo, the Condal and the Victòria, or clubs such as the Bagdad, have put it in the spotlight of the most modern and daring cultural offer of the city.

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city, and it is one of the most popular districts in the Catalan capital. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. Eixample Derecho is home to many gems of 'Modernisme' architecture, including the unique Casa Milà (La Pedrera), the colourful Casa Batlló and the towering Sagr

In addition to these tourist attractions, the area has a wide variety of typical restaurants and bars, such as the Casa Mariol wine cellar, where you can enjoy tapas and wines from the region, or the Japanese restaurant Koy Shunka, one of the best in the city.

neighborhood_overview:
Gràcia is a traditional Catalan neighborhood which enjoys beautiful contrasts.

In it, live neighbors from a long way back together with erasmus students and in the streets mix and mingle bohemian artists, gypsies and different cultures.

It is an area with lots of life and tradition, its neighbors are like a big family. The neighborhood of Gràcia was up until the XIX century an independent town which is why it maintains a very rooted identity.

In its plazas (squares) and streets one breathes tranquility and art. These host several small and independent shops turning a regular walk into an adventure.

The most emblematic places are the Plaza Vila de Gràcia, Plaza del Sol, Casa Vicens, Casa Fuster, Park de la Creueta del Coll and Park Guell.

During the Festivities of Gràcia (end of August – beginning of September) the neighborhood becomes the epicenter of party in Barcelona with street decoration contests and free concerts.

neighborhood_overview:
The Eixample district in Barcelona is renowned for its iconic grid-like layout, designed by Ildefons Cerdà in the 19th century. Characterized by its wide avenues, uniform building heights, and chamfered corners, Eixample is a blend of architectural brilliance and urban functionality.

One of the most notable features of Eixample is its modernista architecture, with gems like Antoni Gaudí's masterpiece, the Sagrada Família, and other remarkable buildings such as Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera). Walking through the streets of Eixample, visitors are treated to a visual feast of ornate facades, intricate ironwork, and colorful mosaics.

Beyond its architectural wonders, Eixample is a bustling commercial and residential hub. The district is dotted with trendy boutiques, cozy cafes, and upscale restaurants, catering to a diverse mix of locals and tourists alike. Its wide sidewalks and numerous squares invite leisurely strolls and al fresco dining experiences.

One of the most notable features of Eixample is its modernista architecture, with gems like Antoni Gaudí's masterpiece, the Sagrada Família, and other remarkable buildings such as Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera). Walking through the streets of Eixample, visitors are treated to a visual feast of ornate facades, intricate ironwork, and colorful mosaics.

Beyond its architectural wonders, Eixample is a bustling commercial and residential hub. The district is dotted with trendy boutiques, cozy cafes, and upscale restaurants, catering to a diverse mix of locals and tourists alike. Its wide sidewalks and numerous squares invite leisurely strolls and al fresco dining experiences.

The presence of Barcelona's finest modernista buildings makes this avenue a veritable open-air museum.

Barcelona's new artery, in the centre of the newly built Eixample district, was the place moneyed bourgeois families chose to live. neighborhood_overview:
Barcelona's Eixample district (Ensanche) was built in the 19th century. The birthplace of the Modernisme art movement, whose main figure is Antoni Gaudí.

This area is home to the impressive Sagrada Familia, famous "La Pedrera", Gaudí's work, the Apple of Discord, Hospital de la Santa Creu and Sant Pau, etc.

A large part of the attraction of the Eixample is the mythical Passeig de Gràcia Avenue, one of Spain's most famous avenues due to its importance in shopping, business, and a great showcase of outstanding works of modernist architecture, comparable to Champs Elysées in Paris or Fifth Avenue in New York.

This area is full of excellent modernist buildings, such as the Casa Batlló de Gaudí, the Casa de Puig i Cadafalch Amatller, and Lleó Morera de Domènech i Muntaner known as the Manzana de la Discordia.

The University of Barcelona is also in this area, an elegant building with beautiful gardens and Casa Gofverichs Boada. A Gaudí collaborator
