description:
Welcome to Rumi's World! I open the doors of my home to anyone who seeks harmony, peace and tranquility.

You will share with me and my plants, this beautiful apartment, located in the Horta neighborhood of Barcelona.

If you are looking for a 5* hotel service and you think that by paying, you have the power to do whatever you want... please don't come to my house... I want to give travelers the opportunity to share and live a local experience, from love and respect as human beings that we are.
neighborhood_overview:
The neighborhood of Horta is, perhaps, one of the corners of Barcelona that still retains its authenticity.

Its privileged position, away from the most central and familiar environments of the city, is allowing its essence and the characteristics that make it unique to continue to remain.

Horta continues to maintain the village air within the big city! It is a “lifelong” neighborhood, where only tourists arrive.
Quiet, safe and authentic area.

Ideal place to rest and visit the city by day. Close to home there is a pharmacy and a "paki" shop that opens from 8h to 22h.

Supermercados a 10 min walk from home, where the subway is.

***ATTENTION* ** Taking the distances as a walk are part of the trip, if you want to have everything close and at your disposal in a minute, sorry to inform you that you will not find it here... In return, you are next to parks and mountains to get lost and discover the REAL BARCELONA.
host_about:
Hola soy Rumi!

Y soy una chica muy abierta de mente, extrovertida, entregada y auténtica. 

Hedonista y sencilla, a la que le gusta mucho el crecimiento personal y espiritual.

Libre de miedos y con pensamiento crítico, me defino como una persona tranquila a la que le gusta estar en casa, dar un buen paseo, leer un buen libro y cocinar bien rico!

Con mucha energía y mucho flow, me gusta conocer gente de todas partes y ayudarles a que se sientan como en casa en una ciudad que no es la suya...

Hablo Inglés, castellano y catalán! Hija de padres argentinos, pero nada y criada en Barcelona, aunque me siento del mundo!

Quiero compartir contigo mi espacio, mi cueva, mi templo. Para que tengas una experiencia familiar y acogedora, dónde te sientas arropado desde el minuto uno, por una persona que no conoces en la ciudad que vas a visitar. Me gustaría que te sientas como en casa, no como un extraño que paga por dormir e irse…

Que podamos compartir momentos y charlas, y que tu estancia pueda fluir de la mejor manera posible, para que sea maravillosa e inolvidable.

¿Te vienes a mi casa y vivir una "Rumi's World Experience"?

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. The Parc de Joan Miró, with its iconic 'Woman and Bird' sculpture created by the Barcelona-born artist, is also situated here, as well as the Arenas

host_about:
El entorno dinámico y alegre de la capital catalana se plasma en The Moods Catedral en forma de experiencia de alojamiento cercana y cálida. Desde el trato de nuestro personal hasta la comodidad de la zona común y nuestras 17 habitaciones, todos los ambientes del hostal tienen mucho de Barcelona y del carácter mediterráneo de sus gentes.

Una idiosincrasia que se percibe ya a la llegada a este hotel del barrio Gótico, donde una recepción con techo de volta catalana con ladrillos en blanco y muebles de líneas sencillas en tonos beige dan la bienvenida al visitante. El pavimento textil en tonos tierra a juego con el minimalismo del mobiliario se conjuga a la perfección con paredes blancas no exentas de vegetación y una presencia omnipresente de la madera. El toque final de bienestar lo aportan las cómodas butacas en tela de lino, un lugar donde descansar o tomar algo.

Esta decoración de diseño llena de guiños a la tierra se reproduce a lo largo de todos y cada uno de los espacios. Colores puros, elementos básicos y geometrías simples se repiten en la zona común de este hotel situado en el límite de los barrios del Gótic y el Born.

En esta zona común, a la cual nos gusta llamar Helpyourself por el servicio gratuito de bebidas al cual tienes acceso durante todo el día, encontrarás también una sala donde hojear algunas de nuestras revistas de moda, tomarte algo, trabajar con tu ordenador o simplemente descansar después de una jornada de turismo en la ciudad.

Asimismo, nuestras 17 luminosas y tranquilas habitaciones han sido creadas en un estilo contemporáneo donde la exclusividad no está reñida con la sencillez.

En The Moods Catedral te transportamos a la mismísima esencia del Mediterráneo.

neighborhood_overview: Sant Antoni is a neighborhood in the Eixample district of Barcelona. Its non-official centre, the marketplace of the same name—designed by Antoni Rovira i Tries and built between 1872 and 1882—is one of the oldest and most popular in the city, especially with the secondhand book stalls that surround the building Sunday mornings. It is bordered by the neighbourhoods of the L’Antiga Esquerra de l’Eixample, the Raval, and Poble Sec. The streets of Sant Antoni follow the grid pattern prevalent in all of Eixample, except for a central thoroughfare, the Avinguda del Mistral built on the site of an important medieval road which led out of Barcelona. Another well-known landmark of Sant Antoni is the bar called Els Tres Tombs, right next to the market.

Gracia offers the choice of quiet sleepy side streets alongside the life and bustle of its squares.

neighborhood_overview:
El Born is a promenade of medieval origin where today there are many trendy terraces. It is a very popular area in Barcelona both during the day and at night and extends between the old Born market and the Gothic church of Santa María del Mar.

El Born is located in the Ribera neighborhood, a labyrinth of alleys that once made up the old artisans' neighborhood and today are home to artists, fashion stores, bars and entertainment venues. neighborhood_overview:
Until the middle of the 19th century, what is now the Sagrada Familia district was a set of agricultural land, on the border of the former independent municipality of San Martín de Provensals with the city of Barcelona. Except for the isolated presence of some farmhouses, it was an unpopulated territory until the sixties of the nineteenth century the first developments began. They were originally humble dwellings - bars and ground floor houses - that were concentrated between what are now the streets of Marina and Paseo de San Juan. This neighborhood was originally known as the El Poblet neighborhood (“the village”), a denomination that was lost during the 20th century in favor of La Sagrada Familia, in reference to the temple, whose works began in 1882.

Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. neighborhood_overview: A modernist treasure trove full of elaborate and often fantastical buildings, elegant landscapes and upmarket fashion - there’s really something magical about Eixample.  The area sits on the right hand side of Passeig de Gràcia, the main boulevard that separates the city.  Its gridded layout keeps things nice and simple for walking around - most tourists flock to Gaudi’s emblematic Sagrada Familia church, but Eixample itself is a peaceful, residential neighbourhood that offers many an opportunity for a quite respite.  You could easily spend the day just popping in-and-out of the various artist galleries, small boutiques and neighbourhood cafes scattered about, that is if you can tear yourself away from the high-end shops that line the avenues.  To top it all off, Eixample is only two metro stops away from Placa Catalunya at the city centre.

Its unofficial center, the market of the same name - designed by Antoni Rovira i Trias and built between 1872 and 1882 - is one of the oldest and largest in the city. The neighborhood is surrounded by the neighborhoods of l'Antiga Esquerra de l'Eixample (across the Gran Vía de les Cortes Catalanes), Raval (across the Ronda de Sant Antoni) and Poble Sec (across the Avinguda del Paral·lel).
The streets of Sant Antoni follow the orthogonal pattern of the widening except for its central avenue, the Avinguda de Mistral, built on an old medieval road out of the city.

neighborhood_overview:
The L'Eixample neighborhood in Barcelona is one of the most emblematic and cosmopolitan in the city. It is known for its modernist architecture and unique urban design, with its famous blocks of square buildings intersecting at right angles.

The L'Eixample district is divided into two parts: the left and the right. The left side is the most commercial, with a wide variety of shops, restaurants and bars. The right part, on the other hand, is more residential and quiet.

L'Eixample is also home to the famous Paseo de Gracia avenue, home to some of Barcelona's most luxurious fashion stores and several of the city's most important modernist buildings, such as Casa Batlló and La Pedrera, designed by the famous architect Antoni Gaudi.

In general, L'Eixample is a very lively and vibrant neighborhood, full of life and activity 24 hours a day. It is a great place to live or visit if you like to be close to the city center and enjoy urban life.

neighborhood_overview:
Gracia used to be a separate town on the edge of Barcelona until it was absorbed by its larger neighbour. It is renowned for the fact that it has always managed to maintain an independent character from the rest of the city.

neighborhood_overview: A modernist treasure trove full of elaborate and often fantastical buildings, elegant landscapes and upmarket fashion - there’s really something magical about Eixample.  The area sits on the right hand side of Passeig de Gràcia, the main boulevard that separates the city.  Its gridded layout keeps things nice and simple for walking around - most tourists flock to Gaudi’s emblematic Sagrada Familia church, but Eixample itself is a peaceful, residential neighbourhood that offers many an opportunity for a quite respite.  You could easily spend the day just popping in-and-out of the various artist galleries, small boutiques and neighbourhood cafes scattered about, that is if you can tear yourself away from the high-end shops that line the avenues.  To top it all off, Eixample is only two metro stops away from Placa Catalunya at the city centre.

neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is conveniently located right by Paseo de Gracia avenue and in the very middle of Eixample district. This elegant, majestic boulevard was a showcase for Barcelona's bourgeoisie at the turn of the 19th century, and links the Plaça Catalunya with the district of Gràcia, hence its name. The presence of Barcelona's finest modernista buildings makes this avenue a veritable open-air museum.

Barcelona's new artery, in the centre of the newly built Eixample district, was the place moneyed bourgeois families chose to live. On either side of the street, they constructed imposing buildings that continue to delight everyone who passes by. These jewels of Catalonia's home-grown art nouveau, modernisme, and the later movement, noucentisme, were created by architects of the calibre of Gaudí (La Pedrera and the Casa Batlló), Puig i Cadafalch (casa Amatller), and Domènech i Muntaner (Casa Lleó Morera), to name just three. We are Abril and Eloi. We are a couple and we are actors- with similar interests.  We like to travel, meet new people from other backgrounds, go to the movies, the theater, museums, watch documentaries, listen to music, going to concerts, reading, dancing, looking after our plants, bike riding (our favorite mode of transportation), trying foods from other countries, cooking mexican-catalan food and  inventing our own dishes. Whenever we have a free weekend, we spend time in the Costa Brava which is only an hour away from the city. The Costa Brava is known for its lush forrest as well as its pristine beaches. Each autumn, you can find us with baskets at the forrest collecting wild mushrooms to make fabulous meals.  

Being hosts in our home is an opportunity to open the door to new experiences and to gain access to what is happening in other latitudes around the world as well as exchanging ideas and different perspectives. neighborhood_overview:
We are located between two neighborhoods: the Sant Pere neighborhood and the L'Exaimple Dreta neighborhood.
Sant Pere, like the adjacent Born district, is a trendy area with old streets lined with alternative boutiques and artisan cafes. Here are the Palau de la Música Catalana, a modernist-style auditorium, and the Santa Caterina market, where Catalan cheeses, seafood and Serrano ham are sold under a huge mosaic-covered roof. At night, young people go out to drink wine and eat gourmet tapas in the bars. There are many excellent art galleries to visit.
Dreta de l'Eixample is a busy neighborhood characterized by its wide avenues with modernist apartment buildings and emblematic buildings by the architect Antoni Gaudí, such as the Sagrada Familia, Casa Batlló and La Pedrera. International boutiques and luxury restaurants abound on Passeig de Gràcia and Rambla de Catalunya. In Plaça de Catalunya there are department stores, cafeterias with terraces and different means of transp
host_about:
We are Abril and Eloi. We are a couple and we are actors- with similar interests.  We like to travel, meet new people from other backgrounds, go to the movies, the theater, museums, watch documentaries, listen to music, going to concerts, reading, dancing, looking after our plants, bike riding (our favorite mode of transportation), trying foods from other countries, cooking mexican-catalan food and  inventing our own dishes. We love to learn new things as well as spending time with our family and friends. We also practice yoga. I am a Hatha Yoga instructor. My partner Eloi enjoys jogging very much.   Whenever we have a free weekend, we spend time in the Costa Brava which is only an hour away from the city. The Costa Brava is known for its lush forrest as well as its pristine beaches. Each autumn, you can find us with baskets at the forrest collecting wild mushrooms to make fabulous meals.  

Being hosts in our home is an opportunity to open the door to new experiences and to gain access to what is happening in other latitudes around the world as well as exchanging ideas and different perspectives. We can learn and enjoy what life has to offer from its vast hues to its lush colors. We would be very happy to show you the beauty of our city and its peoples . Life is about enjoyment and seeing the beauty this world has to offer. Let us be your guide in Barcelona! 


Somos Abril y Eloi, una pareja de actores con intereses muy parecidos. Nos gusta viajar, conocer gente de otras culturas, ir al cine, ir al teatro, museos, ver series, documentales, escuchar música, conciertos, bailar, leer, cuidar de nuestras plantas, andar en bicicleta (nuestro medio de transporte en la ciudad), probar comida de otros lugares, cocinar comida catalo-mexicana e inventar nuevos platillos, estar con la familia, aprender cosas nuevas y disfrutar de los amigos. También practicamos yoga (Abril es profesora de Hatha Yoga) y a Eloi le encanta correr. Cada vez que tenemos oportunidad, generalmente los fines de semana, nos escapamos a la Costa Brava, donde a sólo hora y media de esta ciudad, disfrutamos de sus playas cristalinas y sus bosques (donde cada otoño, nos encontrarás con nuestro cesto bajo el brazo recolectando setas para unas buenas comilonas).
Recibir huéspedes en nuestro hogar, es abrir la puerta a nuevas experiencias, conocer lo que sucede en otras latitudes, intercambiar ideas y visiones distintas, aprender y disfrutar de la vida con sus diversos matices y colores. Estaremos encantados de mostrarte la belleza de nuestra ciudad y su gente. La vida es para disfrutarla plenamente y ver el hermoso mundo en el que vivimos, déjanos ser tu guía en Barcelona!

neighborhood_overview: The Eixample is the Catalan Art Nouveau center of the city. The area was built in the late 19th and early 20th century and the architecture of the neighbourhood is stunning, with some real gems to explore. A few steps from your apartment you’ll be able to feast your eyes on amazing buildings such as Gaudí’s Casa Batlló and the lesser-known but stunning Casa Amatller. The area is one of the cultural and shopping hearts of the city. You’ll find designer stores and high street brands next to all sorts of great restaurants and bars. A short walk (15 minutes) will get you to the bustling old city, where you’ll have another great selection of shops, markets, museums, art galleries, restaurants and bars to choose from. The area boasts great transport links and you’ll be able to get to all ends of the city in a few minutes by subway, bus or taxi.

neighborhood_overview: The neighbourhood of Sants is one of the most emblematic in Barcelona. It was once a small, independent town until the expansion of Barcelona, when it was annexed in 1897. Today, Sants is a residential area with plenty of parks, shops, and restaurants. The main street, Carrer de Sants, is one of Barcelona's biggest commercial avenues, where you can find many shops, markets, and great places for a bite to eat. Choosing to rent an apartment in Sants allows you to immerse yourself among the locals of Barcelona, as tourists do not tend to frequent this area often in comparison with the towns of the inner city. However, Sants is still close to many of the major Barcelona attractions, particularly Plaça d'Espanya and Montjuïc, and you can reach Barcelona's city centre within minutes by metro. Also in the Sants neighbourhood, you will find the Barcelona-Sants Estació train station. From here you can connect easily to all of Barcelona, the El-Prat airport and plenty of the suburbs of the city

Built on the hills, the area used to be where wealthy Barcelonians had their summer residences back in the XIX century. In the 19th century, it was agricultural with country houses, like Mas Guinardó, which gave its name to the neighborhood. In the early 20th century, it consisted of small houses; in the 60s, it transformed into blocks.

Parc Güell stands out in Guinardó. Covering 15.9 hectares, it's one of Barcelona's largest green spaces, offering magnificent views. The Hospital de Sant Pau, a UNESCO World Heritage site, is another architectural gem. Guinardó is residential, with small homes and low-rise buildings (around €4000/m²). Rent averages around €10/m².

This quiet residential neighborhood is located near Parc Güell and offers convenient connections. Guinardó is ideal for families and those seeking a serene space, even though it has less nightlife compared to other areas.

neighborhood_overview:
Guinardó, in Barcelona, is one of the neighborhoods in the Horta-Guinardó district. Its boundaries are: Passeig de Maragall, Carrer de Sant Antoni Maria Claret, Carrer de Cartagena, and Parc del Guinardó. In the 19th century, it was agricultural with country houses, like Mas Guinardó, which gave its name to the neighborhood. In the early 20th century, it consisted of small houses; in the 60s, it transformed into blocks.

Parc Güell stands out in Guinardó. Covering 15.9 hectares, it's one of Barcelona's largest green spaces, offering magnificent views. The Hospital de Sant Pau, a UNESCO World Heritage site, is another architectural gem. Guinardó is residential, with small homes and low-rise buildings (around €4000/m²). Rent averages around €10/m².

This quiet residential neighborhood is located near Parc Güell and offers convenient connections. Guinardó is ideal for families and those seeking a serene space, even though it has less nightlife compared to other areas.

Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. neighborhood_overview: The Eixample is the Catalan Art Nouveau centre of the city. The area was built in the late 19th and early 20th century and the architecture of the neigbourhood is stunning. A few steps from your apartment you’ll be able to feast your eyes on amazing buildings such as Gaudí’s famous, though never finished, church of Sagrada Familia. Other Art Nouveau gems such as Casa Batlló and the lesser-known but impressive Casa Amatller are not far away either. A short walk (15 minutes) will get you to the bustling old city, where you’ll have a great selection of shops, markets, museums, art galleries, restaurants and bars to choose from. The area boasts great transport links and you’ll be able to get to all ends of the city in a few minutes by underground, overground, bus and taxi.

Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. The heart of the buzzing gay club scene is here -- its nickname is even ‘Gaixample’ -- but it has a more laid-back atmosphere than San Francisco’s Castro. You’ll find lively nightlife here, from trendy hipster bars to gilded lounges. Defined by its tree-lined boulevards and Romanesque buildings, the area is full of bustling markets, friendly locals and a wealth of famous attractions, including La Pedrera, the Fundacio Antoni Taples, the Egipci Museum, and the Sala Foundation. If you’re looking to explore Barcelona’s architecture, elegant dining, and nightlife scene, this is the perfect location. neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. The Parc de Joan Miró, with its iconic 'Woman and Bird' sculpture created by the Barcelona-born artist, is also situated here, as well as the Arenas

neighborhood_overview: The neighborhood of Poble Sec was the first extension built outside of Barcelona's historic city centre. Located at the base of Montjuïc, this neighbourhood has great access to all of the attractions on the hill, such as Poble Espanyol and many more museums. The main avenue of Poble Sec is Avinguda Paral·lel, which has been one of the principal areas for activities and leisure since the end of the 19th century. This avenue is home to much of Barcelona's nightlife with bars and clubs dotted along the street, including the popular Sala Apolo. This Barcelona 'Broadway', rich in performance history, is currently laced with numerous theatres including the Victoria Theatre and the Teatre Condal, and is situated close to La Ciutat del Teatre and the Barcelona Teatre Musical, a stage for numerous musicals and dance shows. description:
Charming studio in vibrant, the place where old meets modern. This spacious ground floor loft will welcome you to the POBLE SEC neighborhood.
What else? An interior terrace for those moments of fresh air and reflection.
Located on a quiet street, it will give you the peace you need to disconnect. But be careful! Because just a few steps away, life awakens in a vibrant neighborhood.

neighborhood_overview:
The district Poble Sec lies on the border of Montjüic hill, the backdrop of the World Exposition which took place in Barcelona in 1929 and the Olympic Games in 1992. The most famous street in this district is, Avinguda Paral.lel, which was once the prime centre of Barcelona nightlife - often called the ´Montmartre´ of Barcelona. During the first half of the 20th century, this was Barcelona's area of theatres, nightclubs and music halls.

Today Poble Sec continues to enjoy a friendly atmosphere with quiet streets and parks and you can still find some traditional bars, some more modernized and various good restaurants. You will also notice some modernist buildings along Avinguida Paral.lel that stand out. Poble Sec is also the area with the easiest access to Montjüic park where you can enjoy spectacular views of Barcelona.

The neighborhood of La Vila Olímpica is formed by a series of wide avenues facing the sea. Walking through its streets, along the Paseo Marítim, is the best way to recover the Olympic spirit of the city. And, to regain strength, you can make a visit to any of the terraces that have made this neighborhood a privileged leisure destination. A soft drink and some tapas looking at the sea are Olympic medal!

The Athletes' Neighborhood
The 92 Barcelona Olympics served to orchestrate a deep remodeling in certain areas of the city.

La Vila Olímpica was the official residence of the athletes in Barcelona 92, but the athletes gave way to the families who were settling in the neighborhood, and it became a reference of quality and tranquility in Barcelona. Wide avenues, such as Avenida de Icària or Avenida del Bogatell, fill with light and invite the walk. The main avenue of Poble Sec is Avinguda Paral·lel, which has been one of the principal areas for activities and leisure since the end of the 19th century. This avenue is home to much of Barcelona's nightlife with bars and clubs dotted along the street, including the popular Sala Apolo. neighborhood_overview: Horta/Guinardó is located in the northeast of Barcelona and is one of the largest districts in the city. neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city, and it is one of the most popular districts in the Catalan capital. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. Eixample Derecho is home to many gems of 'Modernisme' architecture, including the unique Casa Milà (La Pedrera), the colourful Casa Batlló and the towering Sagr

Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. The Parc de Joan Miró, with its iconic 'Woman and Bird' sculpture created by the Barcelona-born artist, is also situated here, as well as the Arenas

neighborhood_overview:
Welcome to Casa Wilson, nestled in the vibrant Gràcia neighborhood just a stones throw from Plaça Rovira i Trias, a charming hub that captures both the history and energy of Barcelona. Named after Antoni Rovira i Trias, a celebrated local architect and urban planner, the square honors him with a life-sized bronze sculpture seated on a bench, overlooking the area he helped design. Known also as Plaça dels Tres Senyors, this square reflects old Gràcia, when it was a village surrounded by rural lands owned by three prominent families.
Beyond the square, Gràcia’s bohemian spirit and artistic flair come to life. Winding streets are filled with boutique shops, cozy cafés, and bustling markets where locals and visitors alike enjoy the lively yet relaxed pace of life. With vibrant plazas where musicians, artists, and neighbors gather, Gràcia feels like a small town within the city—a place that’s warm, welcoming, and full of charm.

With 34,000 m² it is the second largest square in Spain,1 after the Plaza de España in Madrid, and ahead of the Plaza de Catalunya in Barcelona.

It is an important transit center of the city, when the Gran Vía de las Cortes Catalanas, Avenida del Paralelo, Calle Tarragona, Calle Creu Coberta and Avenida de la Reina María Cristina converge, through which the Montjuïc area is accessed, and where the Sample Fair and the National Art Museum of Catalonia are located.

neighborhood_overview: Sant Antoni is a neighborhood in the Eixample district of Barcelona. Its non-official centre, the marketplace of the same name—designed by Antoni Rovira i Tries and built between 1872 and 1882—is one of the oldest and most popular in the city, especially with the secondhand book stalls that surround the building Sunday mornings. It is bordered by the neighbourhoods of the L’Antiga Esquerra de l’Eixample, the Raval, and Poble Sec. The streets of Sant Antoni follow the grid pattern prevalent in all of Eixample, except for a central thoroughfare, the Avinguda del Mistral built on the site of an important medieval road which led out of Barcelona. Another well-known landmark of Sant Antoni is the bar called Els Tres Tombs, right next to the market.

neighborhood_overview: The Esquerra de l’Eixample, or Left of Extension in Catalan, is separated into two sections: old and modern, which is where Entença is located. The style of Old Left Eixample is largely Neo-Romanesque, and visitors are encouraged to take a stroll through the neighborhood to observe the wonderful architecture. The Universitat de Barcelona and the Plaça de la Universitat, both of which are only a few minutes’ walk from the flat, are good instances of this. They will also come across The Mercat de Sant Antoni, the Ninot, where they may purchase some goods. New Left Eixample was built in the 1930s and is more of a Monderisme style. Close by are the Casa Batlló, the Escola Industrial, the Modelo Prison, and the Escorxador Slaughterhouses. These structures, on the other hand, were built before the neighborhood was even conceived.

neighborhood_overview:
Gràcia is a district in Barcelona which gathers the charm of tradition with the freshness of modernity. It was once an independent town. However, nowadays, it is the core of a district that includes other neighbourhoods such as Vallcarca Pentitents or Salut. All this area is very popular for its nightlife. You can also find a great number of boutiques and a variety of bars and restaurants.


The district of Gràcia is home to many students. There is as well a community of artists, actors, musicians, photographers and designers. They all contribute to the “bohemian” environment which is characteristic of the place. You can easily access the most emblematic places of the city from here (the Casa Fuster, Parc Guell, Casa Vicens, Paseo de Gracia, Gracia squares, etc.).

Perfectly situated between Plaça Catalunya, El Born and Eixample, it offers walking access to all main attractions while maintaining the quiet, secure atmosphere of a well-kept residential street with good lighting and regular police presence.

Unlike other central areas that may be noisier or more tourist-heavy (like the Raval or parts of the Gothic Quarter), this neighborhood features quality buildings, local cafés, boutiques and a relaxed, authentic vibe. Ideal for families, couples and travelers looking for both convenience and peace of mind.

- Metro and train stations (L1, L3, RENFE) within 3 minutes.

Lodging Team

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city, and it is one of the most popular districts in the Catalan capital. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. name: Authentic Gem in Quaint Market Plaza in Barcelona
description: This flat was fully reburbished last year.  It´s location is unbeatable, with a small balcony over looking Sant Andreu´s amazingly quiet plaza and marketplace.  High ceilings and fully restored unique wooden beams are seen throughout the flat.  The kitchen´s flooring of modernist style tiles are maintained, while containing all the modern day conveniences. host_about:
I am originally from Vietnam and had been raised in Southern California, but now have been living in Barcelona for the past 25 years and consider it my first home.

I quit my stressful job some years back and since am collaborating in two NGO projects, ones which I enjoy and find tremendously fulfilling.  

Places that I have particularly fond memories from visiting them are:  Maui, Trinidad & Tobago, Tuscany, Cambodia, Morocco, Istanbul and the Ivory Coast.  

I love the beauty of nature and particularly appreciate flowers, divine trees, mesmerising waterfalls, prestine lakes, etc.  My idea of an amazing day would be a scenic drive leading up an outdoor picnic, and having plenty of time then to sky and star daze and to discover new routes to trek and hidden pools to dunk into.

English is my most fluent language, followed by Spanish, Vietnamese and Catalan.  I have been trying to learn to speak French forever, but I think I will be stuck at the Beginner´s level unless I go to live there for a substantial period of time.

neighborhood_overview:
Modern Barcelona was born in L’Eixample, devised by the engineer and urban planner to whom he owes his magical and unique drawing: Ildefons Cerdà. With its urban plan, Cerdà designed an egalitarian city, where neighborhoods are not differentiated from others and public services are distributed evenly throughout every corner.

The district is the result of one of the most splendid moments in the city's history, when it is definitely configured as the engine of contemporary Catalonia and breaks with the medieval past knocking down the walls. L’Eixample was built in the years of the industrialization of Catalonia, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The central part, the Dreta de l'Eixample, was the bourgeoisie neighborhood that introduced into its home a style of its own, modernism.

L’Eixample is formed by six neighborhoods: La Dreta de l’Eixample, Old Esquerra de l’Eixample, Nova Esquerra de l’Eixample, Fort Pienc, Sagrada Família and Sant Antoni.

Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. The main avenue of Poble Sec is Avinguda Paral·lel, which has been one of the principal areas for activities and leisure since the end of the 19th century. This avenue is home to much of Barcelona's nightlife with bars and clubs dotted along the street, including the popular Sala Apolo. name: Modern and Spacious Apartment in Eixample
description: Spacious and elegant apartment with five bedrooms and four bathrooms, ideal for groups of up to 10 people. Located in the central Eixample district, just a short walk from the old town and well connected to the rest of the city. Its modern and bright design features high ceilings and light-toned decor. It includes Wi-Fi, satellite TV, and a fully equipped kitchen, perfect for a comfortable and functional stay.
neighborhood_overview: The Eixample is the center of modernism (the Catalan Art Nouveau) of the city. The area was built in the late 19th century and 20th century princioios and the architecture of the neighborhood is impressive: a few steps from the apartment you can enjoy incredible buildings such as Gaudí's Casa Batlló and the lesser known but impressive Casa Amatller. The area is one of the cultural and commercial centers of the city. Here you will find designer and brand stores next to all kinds of restaurants and bars. A short walk (5 minutes) will take you to the bustling old town, where you will have another great selection of shops, markets, museums, art galleries, restaurants and bars. The area has great transport links and you can get to all the ends of the city in a few minutes by subway, bus and taxi.

It is a neighborhood with a discreet but attractive nightlife, with several bars and restaurants offering a wide gastronomic offer. It is also known for its proximity to green areas, such as Turó Park, perfect for relaxing outdoors. Sant Gervasi-Galvany is popular with families and professionals looking for a quiet lifestyle without being far from the urban activity of Barcelona.

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city, and it is one of the most popular districts in the Catalan capital. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. The street is intersected by the long Avinguda Diagonal, which runs through the entire city. Eixample Derecho is home to many gems of 'Modernisme' architecture, including the unique Casa Milà (La Pedrera), the colourful Casa Batlló and the towering Sagr

neighborhood_overview: Horta/Guinardó is located in the northeast of Barcelona and is one of the largest districts in the city. The area is significantly more tranquil than the bustling towns of the city centre, although it is easy to reach all of the sights in Barcelona by bus or metro from this corner of the Catalan capital. The area is known for its steep hills, as part of Horta-Guinardó lies on the Collserola Mountain range. You will also find the lovely Parc del Laberint d'Horta in this district, which is Barcelona's oldest garden, featuring a labyrinth made up of 750 cypress trees. If you're looking for a quieter base for your trip to Barcelona, without venturing too far from the main sights and attractions of the city, then an apartment in Horta-Guinardó is an ideal choice.

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. The Parc de Joan Miró, with its iconic 'Woman and Bird' sculpture created by the Barcelona-born artist, is also situated here, as well as the Arenas

neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. The Parc de Joan Miró, with its iconic 'Woman and Bird' sculpture created by the Barcelona-born artist, is also situated here, as well as the Arenas

neighborhood_overview: The Esquerra de l’Eixample, or Left of Extension in Catalan, is separated into two sections: old and modern, which is where Entença is located. The style of Old Left Eixample is largely Neo-Romanesque, and visitors are encouraged to take a stroll through the neighborhood to observe the wonderful architecture. The Universitat de Barcelona and the Plaça de la Universitat, both of which are only a few minutes’ walk from the flat, are good instances of this. They will also come across The Mercat de Sant Antoni, the Ninot, where they may purchase some goods. New Left Eixample was built in the 1930s and is more of a Monderisme style. Close by are the Casa Batlló, the Escola Industrial, the Modelo Prison, and the Escorxador Slaughterhouses. These structures, on the other hand, were built before the neighborhood was even conceived.

Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample was designed by Catalan-born urban planning visionary, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when creating the plans for this new district. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. neighborhood_overview: Eixample is Catalan for 'extension', meaning an extension of the old Barcelona city. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), both of which are home to some fantastic restaurants and stores. Eixample Izquierdo is delimited by the grand, Passeig de Gràcia, a paradise for shopping and dining, and Plaça d'Espanya, where the Montjuïc Magic Fountain and one of the biggest convention centres in Barcelona can be found. neighborhood_overview: The Esquerra de l’Eixample, or Left of Extension in Catalan, is separated into two sections: old and modern, which is where Entença is located. The style of Old Left Eixample is largely Neo-Romanesque, and visitors are encouraged to take a stroll through the neighborhood to observe the wonderful architecture. The Universitat de Barcelona and the Plaça de la Universitat, both of which are only a few minutes’ walk from the flat, are good instances of this. They will also come across The Mercat de Sant Antoni, the Ninot, where they may purchase some goods. New Left Eixample was built in the 1930s and is more of a Monderisme style. Close by are the Casa Batlló, the Escola Industrial, the Modelo Prison, and the Escorxador Slaughterhouses. These structures, on the other hand, were built before the neighborhood was even conceived.

Eixample was designed by Catalan-born architect, Ildefons Cerdà, who took traffic and sunlight (amongst many other things) into consideration when drawing up the plans of the new area. Eixample is now characterised by its octagonal blocks and its grid-like pattern, with wide streets and both commercial and residential areas. It is split into two parts, Eixample Esquerra (Left, or in Spanish, Izquierdo) and Eixample Dret (Right, or in Spanish, Derecho), and is home to one of the most famous streets in Barcelona, Passeig de Gràcia, known for its high fashion stores and trendy restaurants. Lodging Team
